quotes.quote: When you create a **FastAPI** application, there is a `webhooks` attribute that you can use to define *webhooks*, the same way you would define *path operations*, for example with `@app.webhooks.post()`.

nuggets.text: Declare webhooks with the app's webhooks attribute the same way as path operations, using a decorator such as @app.webhooks.post(...).

quotes.quote: Notice that with webhooks you are actually not declaring a *path* (like `/items/`), the text you pass there is just an **identifier** of the webhook (the name of the event), for example in `@app.webhooks.post("new-subscription")`, the webhook name is `new-subscription`.

nuggets.text: The string passed is not a URL path: it is only an identifier of the webhook, the name of the event (e.g. new-subscription).

quotes.quote: The webhooks that you define will end up in the **OpenAPI** schema and the automatic **docs UI**.

nuggets.text: Webhooks defined this way end up in the OpenAPI schema and the automatic docs UI.

quotes.quote: This is because it is expected that **your users** would define the actual **URL path** where they want to receive the webhook request in some other way (e.g. a web dashboard).

nuggets.text: The actual URL path where the webhook request is received is expected to be defined by your users some other way, such as a web dashboard.

quotes.quote: The `app.webhooks` object is actually just an `APIRouter`, the same type you would use when structuring your app with multiple files.

nuggets.text: app.webhooks is just an APIRouter, the same type used when structuring an app with multiple files.

nuggets.text: Pass the dict type as response_model in the path operation decorator, e.g. response_model=dict[str, float].

quotes.quote: In these cases you can configure the server with `fastapi run --root-path`.

To achieve this, you can use the command line option `--root-path` like:

```console
$ uv run fastapi run main.py --forwarded-allow-ips="*" --root-path /api/v1

nuggets.text: Start the server with the --root-path option set to the prefix the proxy strips (here /billing), e.g. fastapi run main.py --root-path /billing.

quotes.quote: But then, when you open the integrated docs UI (the frontend), it would expect to get the OpenAPI schema at `/openapi.json`, instead of `/api/v1/openapi.json`.

nuggets.text: Without it, the docs UI requests the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json instead of at the prefixed path (e.g. /billing/openapi.json).

quotes.quote: The docs UI would also need the OpenAPI schema to declare that this API `server` is located at `/api/v1` (behind the proxy).

nuggets.text: The docs UI also needs the OpenAPI schema to declare that the API server is located at the prefix (a servers entry with url /billing).

quotes.quote: The `root_path` is a mechanism provided by the ASGI specification (that FastAPI is built on, through Starlette).

The ASGI specification defines a `root_path` for this use case.

And the `--root-path` command line option provides that `root_path`.

nuggets.text: The --root-path option provides the ASGI root_path, a mechanism the ASGI specification defines for this use case.

quotes.quote: The limit applies to the **whole request body**. If you upload two files in the same request, both files, any form fields, and the bytes used to encode the multipart form all count toward that one limit.

nuggets.text: No, the limit is not per file: it applies to the whole request body, so all the uploaded files in one request count together toward that single limit.

quotes.quote: any form fields, and the bytes used to encode the multipart form all count toward that one limit. The URL and request headers are outside the body.

nuggets.text: Form fields and the bytes used to encode the multipart form also count toward the limit, while the URL and request headers do not.

quotes.quote: If a read exceeds the limit, FastAPI stops reading and returns an HTTP **413 Content Too Large** response if the response hasn't started yet.

quotes.quote: Use `max_body_size` to bound the whole request, including uploaded file contents.

quotes.quote: Exceeding a parser limit returns HTTP 400.

nuggets.text: Exceeding one of the form parser limits set in form_limits (max_fields, max_files, max_part_size) returns HTTP 400, not 413.
